quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What effect does shifting to a lower gear have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. When you shift to a lower gear, it slows you down.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should the passenger do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on the motorcycle only after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail.

questions.question: Why should you maintain a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: So you have time and space to see and react to hazards.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
So other drivers will cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you have time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of hazards like potholes.

questions.question: What happens to steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: There is no change in steering.

questions.explanation: If your front tire fails, the steering will feel heavy. If steering feels heavy, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road condition is.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You cannot see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset its balance.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Help you be seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. You should NOT try to avoid being seen.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, get close, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, get close, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, shift to a lower gear and slow down to approach the dog. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not kick it.

questions.question: What lessens the effects of alcohol after drinking?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. You cannot speed up this process. Only time will lessen alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes more firmly than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes more softly than usual to keep from overworking them.

questions.explanation: A passenger in a sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. This affects how it handles and stops. Your motorcycle will need more distance to stop completely.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation works better on straightaways.

questions.question: Before riding, perform all of these checks except:

options.text: Test both brake controls to ensure the brake light activates.
Ensure the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, and fluid levels. Also check that your headlights, taillight, turn signals, and brake light all work.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Ride in the part of your lane that other drivers will see you first.
Always stay in the left lane to be farthest from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of your lane that other drivers will see you first.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in your lane so other drivers see you as soon as possible. For example, when approaching a blind corner on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are regulatory signs. They are white with black lettering and show rules like speed limits. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the operator:
questions.explanation: Operators can use hand signals instead of turn signals. A left arm extended straight out to the left means the operator plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straightaway.
More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
Done safely by using the front brake only.
Done safely by using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Wobbles are usually caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for either protection.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding in fog?

options.text: Alternate between the low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: Which one is not protective riding gear?

options.text: Boots that go above the ankle
Pants made of a soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of a soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket, sturdy pants, ankle-covering boots, and hearing protection. Soft material pants do not provide adequate protection.
